body:
(Issue opened during a discussion between Elar and Josh)

V10 has historically been about "malicious" code.

With section 10.4, the focus shifted to how to write code correctly from a security perspective. Not just code quality but things that if you don't do, you are probably insecure.

It has been suggested that V10 needs to be refocused to be more like: "Secure Coding Architecture and Implementation."

The idea being, this is for requirements that don't necessarily relate to a particular area of security like authentication or access control and don't necessarily relate to a particular type of application functionality such as a logging or file handling.

For now:

* The 10.4 defensive coding definitely belongs in here
* 10.1 has been eliminated
* 10.2 (malicious code) will probably be cut down/simplified and in any case seems to fit ok here. 
* 10.3 (application integrity) needs to be reviewed and may have requirements removed or moved.
* We would probably need to add an architecture section to this chapter.
* There is an open question as to whether 14.2 (dependency security) should be moved here as the requirements are a little more relevant to here than to configuration.

(FYI @ImanSharaf)
